text:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV2 - multiple nodes in inference-pool-usw reporting NotReady / kubelet restart loops (4 nodes). Trigger: node-heartbeat-miss x3 in 2m. Link: https://incidents/redwood/5198765432 :rotating_light:

sam_oncall: saw it, grabbing context. marking myself as PRIMARY.

priya_sre: i'm on GPU-driver + kubelet logs, joining...

darren_runtime: getting live traces from runtime agents, seeing repeated `OOMKilled` for inference-container + `NVRM: GPU reset` lines in dmesg on two nodes.

elena_ops: can we cordon/drain the affected nodes? want to avoid churn across the pool.

sam_oncall: yes cordon first, drain if eviction doesn't resolve. runbook step 3.

priya_sre: paste: ```
# tail -n 30 /var/log/kubelet.log
I0512 18:14:02 kubelet.go:... heartbeat missed, restarting kubelet
E0512 18:14:03 kubelet: pod "inference-worker-..." OOMKilled
Kernel: NVRM: GPU at GPU-0: GPU has fallen off the bus
```

maya_support: product metrics: errors up 2.8% for hosted generation endpoints in US-W, p95 latency +320ms. A few customers flagged elevated 500s.

priya_sre: running `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady` ->```
ip-10-0-34-12 NotReady  2d  nvidia.com/gpu=1
ip-10-0-35-14 NotReady  3m  nvidia.com/gpu=1
ip-10-0-36-21 NotReady  1m  nvidia.com/gpu=1
ip-10-0-40-09 NotReady  10s nvidia.com/gpu=1
```

darren_runtime: looks like a cascading GPU reset -> kubelet restart -> pods evicted -> cluster autoscaler tries to replace -> new nodes join then get same reset. repop loop.

elena_ops: action plan: 1) cordon the 4 nodes 2) scale up a small set of standby nodes in eu-west/us-central as overflow 3) route traffic off US-W failover pool via routing policy.

sam_oncall: doing #1 now -> `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-34-12` -> ``Node "ip-10-0-34-12" cordoned``

priya_sre: filing quick mitigation: pin inference workloads to alternative pool via annotation for 5m and start drain: ``kubectl drain ip-10-0-34-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`` -> some pods failed to terminate due to gpu device plugin; killing container runtime on node to force eviction.

maya_support: routing change in progress, reducing inbound to inference-pool-usw by ~60%, notifying customers on affected endpoints: message queued.

darren_runtime: quick fix idea: force scheduler to use quantized/model-small variant by toggling model routing flag for hosted-api for US-W: `redwood route set --region us-west --model small-quant --weight 1.0` — will reduce GPU stress per request.

elena_ops: started scale up in us-central: `kops scale --group infer-pool-standby --replicas 12` -> new nodes healthy.

sam_oncall: good. escalating to eng-sre/pager for deeper root cause. @priya, can you confirm driver/OS versions?

priya_sre: nodes showing nvidia-driver 535.86 and kernel 6.1.11; two nodes show recent apt upgrade applied ~2h ago. suspect driver/kernel mismatch. collecting kernel logs and dmesg.

darren_runtime: attaching small excerpt from GPU logs: ```
[ 2345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, ... GPC0/TSG1 
[ 2345.679002] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 2345.680123] oom-kill: Killed process 4123 (inference-runner) total-vm:358324kB
```

maya_support: customers on /v1/generate in US-W showing retries and 500s; support is triaging three customers with elevated SLA risk.

sam_oncall: declare SEV2, notify oncall rotation to eng-sre channel. putting blameless note.

priya_sre: mitigation verdict: coordinate with infra to rollback the apt upgrade on kernel or pin drivers. for immediate safety, we've drained affected nodes and put a temporary taint `no-infer-join=true:NoSchedule` on new nodes until driver validated.

elena_ops: added taint and updated node pool autoscaling to prefer standby pool. routing reroute confirmed by gateway logs.

darren_runtime: enacted model fallback; CPU overhead up but GPU pressure reduced. error rates dropping to 0.6% after 7m.

maya_support: updating status page: "Partial degradation in US-West inference services. Routing in place. Engineers investigating GPU driver-related node resets."

sam_oncall: handoff in 20m to night shift. will capture all artifacts into incident ticket INC-20240512-03. please add follow-ups: (a) kernel/driver compatibility check across fleet (b) gating apt upgrades with preflight driver tests (c) extend node healthchecks to detect NVRM resets quicker.

priya_sre: creating a short reproducer on staging with driver 535.86 + kernel 6.1.x, scheduling heavy inference load. will post link to PR/issue.

elena_ops: removing cordon/taints from nodes once driver rollback validated.

darren_runtime: final note: suspect sequence: recent kernel update + driver edge build -> GPU reset -> kubelet restart -> pod evictions -> autoscaler thrash -> repeated node flaps.

sam_oncall: thanks team. moving to monitor / close once metrics stable for 30 min and customers notified. :white_check_mark:

maya_support: will follow up with affected customers with timeline and post-incident remediation plan.

incident-bot: NOTE: SEV2 incident created INC-20240512-03. responders: sam_oncall, priya_sre, darren_runtime, elena_ops.

sam_oncall: last check: p95 latency down to +40ms, error rate 0.2% US-W. handing off to night oncall in 18m.

priya_sre: adding remediation owner: priya_sre -> tracking issue: https://issues/redwood/2345
